title: Availability Attacks Create Shortcuts

problem.claim: Availability attacks aim to prevent unauthorized machine-learning use by poisoning training data with imperceptible perturbations.

gap.claim: The work investigates why availability-attack perturbations work in principle.

contributions.claim: The perturbations used in availability attacks are almost linearly separable when assigned the target labels of their corresponding samples, allowing them to function as shortcuts for the learning objective.
Linear separability is the workhorse of availability attacks.
Linearly separable perturbations can be synthesized as attacks and are reported to be as powerful as deliberately crafted attacks while being easier to generate.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that they are the first to unveil the population property that availability-attack perturbations are almost linearly separable when assigned the corresponding target labels.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that synthetic linearly separable perturbations are as powerful as deliberately crafted attacks.
The authors report that their algorithm generates ImageNet perturbations in several seconds, whereas previous attacks require dozens of hours.
The authors report that shortcut learning may be more widely present than previously believed, including when shortcuts are imperceptible and mixed with normal features.

narrative_sequence.summary: Availability attacks poison training data with imperceptible perturbations to prevent unauthorized machine-learning use.
The work investigates the principle underlying the effectiveness of these perturbations.
The perturbations are almost linearly separable under corresponding target labels and can act as shortcuts for learning.
The authors synthesize linearly separable perturbations, report comparable attack power and easier generation, and give an ImageNet generation-time example.
The finding suggests shortcut learning may occur more broadly, even with imperceptible shortcuts mixed with normal features.

source_observation.claim: Availability-attack perturbations can be almost linearly separable under the samples' target labels and serve as shortcuts for the learning objective.

interpretation.claim: A model may preferentially use a simple, separable signal even when that signal is imperceptible and mixed with ordinary features.

application.claim: When analyzing model behavior or data-poisoning defenses, test whether an unintended or adversarial feature is linearly separable and can dominate the learning objective.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this shortcut behavior generalizes across datasets, architectures, or training settings beyond the reported findings.

source_observation.claim: Synthetic linearly separable perturbations are reported to be as powerful as deliberately crafted attacks and much easier to generate.

interpretation.claim: Attack construction may be simplified by targeting a separable shortcut rather than optimizing a more complex perturbation.

application.claim: For robustness evaluations, compare attack effectiveness and generation cost for simple synthetic perturbations against deliberately crafted attacks.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the evaluation scope or conditions supporting the reported equivalence in attack power.

unknowns: Datasets, model architectures, training procedures, and evaluation metrics are not specified.
The abstract does not describe perturbation construction details or threat-model assumptions.
The abstract does not provide independent verification of the reported findings.
